Somerville.narrative: Somerville remains one of Greater Boston's most fiercely competitive markets, with condos leading the charge at a median sale price of $972,500 and a remarkable 44.6% of units selling above asking price at exactly 100% of list price on average — a clear signal that demand is overwhelming available supply. Single families and multi-families aren't far behind, fetching medians of $1,175,000 and $1,238,000 respectively, with roughly 1 in 4 homes in each category closing over ask. With inventory so tight that months of supply is effectively zero across all property types and only 75 total sales recorded in the past 30 days, sellers hold an extraordinary advantage and can expect strong, fast offers with minimal concessions. Buyers need to come in fully prepared — pre-approved, flexible on terms, and ready to bid aggressively — as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,475,000 and an astonishing 76.9% of properties selling above asking price at an average of 104.2% of list price — a clear signal that demand is vastly outpacing available inventory. The condo market, while more accessible at a $998,000 median, is no less intense, with 71 units closing in the past 30 days and 38% still trading over asking at exactly list-price parity on average, suggesting sellers are pricing more strategically to capture multiple offers. Multi-family properties are also moving briskly at a $2,029,000 median, with 30% selling above ask, making them an attractive but increasingly expensive play for investor-buyers eyeing Cambridge's perennially strong rental demand. For sellers, the near-zero months of supply across all property types means now is an exceptional time to list, while buyers should expect to bring their strongest offers — waived contingencies, escalation clauses, and pre-inspections are effectively table stakes in this market.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $887,500 and an eye-popping 104.7% sale-to-list ratio — nearly 69% of homes selling above asking price in the past 30 days. Condos are holding steady at $629,000 with half of buyers still paying over list, while multi-families are commanding a median of $1,134,000, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. With effectively zero months of supply across the board and only 31 total sales in the last 30 days, inventory is essentially nonexistent, signaling an intensely supply-starved market. Sellers are in an exceptional position to command premium prices and favorable terms, while buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and the flexibility to move quickly — hesitation in Medford right now is costly.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose remains a fiercely competitive market across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,003,250 and selling at a remarkable 110.3% of list price — with 85% of homes closing above asking, buyers need to come prepared with aggressive offers and minimal contingencies. Multi-family properties are equally in demand, with a median sale price of $1,341,000 and 60% selling over ask, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant interest in this well-connected suburb. The condo segment offers a comparatively more accessible entry point at a $385,000 median, though even there two-thirds of units are selling above list price. With essentially no months of supply across all categories and only 28 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight — sellers are in an exceptionally strong position, while buyers should expect multiple-offer scenarios and should be ready to move quickly and decisively.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes posting a median sale price of $1,228,555 and a staggering 107.7% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying well above asking, with 84.6% of homes selling over list price in the past 30 days. Multi-family properties are equally hot at a $1,350,000 median with 80% of sales closing above ask, while condos offer a comparatively softer entry point at $854,000, though even there, over a third of units are attracting above-list offers. With essentially zero months of supply across all categories and 40 total transactions closed in the last 30 days, inventory is critically tight, signaling that demand is dramatically outpacing what's available. Sellers in Arlington are in an exceptionally strong position to command premium prices and favorable terms, while buyers should expect intense competition, waived contingencies, and the need to move decisively — coming in at or well above asking price is virtually a prerequisite to winning in this market.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,452,000 and closing at 103.8% of list price — 66.7% of those homes selling above asking within the past 30 days. Multi-family properties are even hotter, with a striking 108% sale-to-list ratio and 80% of the 5 sales closing over ask at a median of $1,400,000, signaling strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing assets. Condos offer a comparatively softer entry point at $775,000 with a 99% sale-to-list ratio, though even that segment sees 1 in 5 units trading above ask. For sellers, razor-thin inventory and zero months of supply mean exceptional leverage to command premium pricing, while buyers should expect swift decisions, escalation clauses, and likely waived contingencies to remain competitive in this high-demand suburb.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a $975,000 median sale price and an eye-catching 103.3% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying well above asking, with two-thirds of homes selling over list price. Condos are moving briskly at a $705,000 median with half of units fetching above asking, while multi-family properties are commanding a $1,152,500 median, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing assets. With effectively zero months of supply across all categories and 35 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight, leaving buyers with little negotiating leverage and virtually no room to hesitate. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced homes are generating immediate, above-ask offers — while buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and the flexibility to move quickly in what remains one of Boston's most supply-constrained suburban markets.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's real estate market remains exceptionally competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,445,075 and selling at 101.2% of list price, while half of all homes sold above asking — a clear signal that buyers should expect multiple-offer scenarios and come prepared to act decisively. The condo segment is even more cutthroat, with 83.3% of units closing over list price at a striking 103.7% sale-to-list ratio and a median of $1,044,000, suggesting that even the traditionally "more attainable" entry point in Winchester requires aggressive offers. With essentially no months of supply recorded across all categories and 18 single-family homes sold in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it appears, leaving buyers with little time to deliberate. For sellers, conditions are about as favorable as the market gets — pricing at or slightly below market value is a proven strategy to generate competitive bidding and achieve well above-ask results.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single families commanding a median of $895,500 and selling at exactly list price on average, while a striking 51.6% of homes closed above asking — a clear signal that buyers should expect bidding wars and come prepared with strong offers and minimal contingencies. The condo market is equally active with 336 units sold in the past 30 days at a $802,500 median, and though the sale-to-list ratio of 99.5% suggests slightly less pressure than single families, one in three condos still sold over ask, leaving little room for negotiation. Multi-family properties are the priciest segment at a $1,137,500 median, selling at full list price with 46.6% going above ask, making them a hot commodity for investors and owner-occupants alike who are drawn to Boston's strong rental demand. With essentially no months of supply reported across all categories, this is an unmistakably seller's market — owners listing today hold tremendous leverage, while buyers must act decisively, get pre-approved, and be ready to waive contingencies to compete.
